name: AbstractRange
overview: ["The AbstractRange abstract interface is the base class upon which all DOM range types are defined. A range is an object that indicates the start and end points of a section of content within the document.","As an abstract interface, you will not directly instantiate an object of type AbstractRange. Instead, you will use the Range or StaticRange interfaces. To understand the difference between those two interfaces, and how to choose which is appropriate for your needs."]

properties.name: collapsed
properties.overview: A Boolean value which is true if the range is collapsed. A collapsed range is one whose start position and end position are the same, resulting in a zero-character-long range.

properties.name: endContainer
properties.overview: The DOM Node in which the end of the range, as specified by the endOffset property, is located.

properties.name: endOffset
properties.overview: An integer value indicating the offset, in characters, from the beginning of the node's contents to the beginning of the range represented by the range object. This value must be less than the length of the endContainer node.

properties.name: startContainer
properties.overview: The DOM Node in which the beginning of the range, as specified by the startOffset property, is located.

properties.name: startOffset
properties.overview: An integer value indicating the offset, in characters, from the beginning of the node's contents to the last character of the contents referred to  by the range object. This value must be less than the length of the node indicated in startContainer.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. name: Attr
overview: ["The Attr interface represents one of a DOM element's attributes as an object. In most DOM methods, you will directly retrieve the attribute as a string (e.g., Element.getAttribute()), but certain functions (e.g., Element.getAttributeNode()) or means of iterating return Attr types."]

properties.name: localName
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the local part of the qualified name of the attribute.

properties.name: name
properties.overview: The attribute's name.

properties.name: namespaceURI
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the namespace URI of the attribute, or null if there is no namespace.

properties.name: ownerElement
properties.overview:
The element holding the attribute.

Note: DOM Level 4 removed this property. The assumption was that since you get an Attr object from an Element, you should already know the associated element.
As that doesn't hold true in cases like Attr objects being returned by Document.evaluate, the DOM Living Standard reintroduced the property.

Gecko outputs a deprecation note starting from Gecko 7.0 (Firefox 7.0 / Thunderbird 7.0 / SeaMonkey 2.4). This note was removed again in Gecko 49.0 (Firefox 49.0 / Thunderbird 49.0 / SeaMonkey 2.46).

properties.name: prefix
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the namespace prefix of the attribute, or null if no prefix is specified.

properties.name: specified
properties.overview: This property always returns true. Originally, it returned true if the attribute was explicitly specified in the source code or by a script, and false if its value came from the default one defined in the document's DTD.

properties.name: value
properties.overview: The attribute's value.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.name: other
parameters.overview: The other Node with which to compare the first node’s document position.

parameters.name: otherNode

methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the prefix for a given namespace URI, if present, and null if not. When multiple prefixes are possible, the result is implementation-dependent.

parameters.name: child

name: AudioTrack
overview: ["The AudioTrack interface represents a single audio track from one of the HTML media elements, element is used to embed sound content in documents. It may contain one or more audio sources, represented using the src attribute or the element: the browser will choose the most suitable one. It can also be the destination for streamed media, using a MediaStream.\"><audio> or ) embeds a media player which supports video playback into the document. You can use . The most common use for accessing an AudioTrack object is to toggle its enabled property in order to mute and unmute the track."]

properties.name: enabled
properties.overview: A Boolean value which controls whether or not the audio track's sound is enabled. Setting this value to false mutes the track's audio.

properties.name: id
properties.overview: A DOMString which uniquely identifies the track within the media. This ID can be used to locate a specific track within an audio track list by calling AudioTrackList.getTrackById(). The ID can also be used as the fragment part of the URL if the media supports seeking by media fragment per the Media Fragments URI specification.

properties.name: kind
properties.overview: A DOMString specifying the category into which the track falls. For example, the main audio track would have a kind of "main".

properties.name: label
properties.overview: A DOMString providing a human-readable label for the track. For example, an audio commentary track for a movie might have a label of "Commentary with director John Q. Public and actors John Doe and Jane Eod." This string is empty if no label is provided.

properties.name: language
properties.overview: A DOMString specifying the audio track's primary language, or an empty string if unknown. The language is specified as a BCP 47 (RFC 5646) language code, such as "en-US" or "pt-BR".

name: AudioTrackList
overview: ["The AudioTrackList interface is used to represent a list of the audio tracks contained within a given HTML media element, with each track represented by a separate or object in the list.","Retrieve an instance of this object with HTMLMediaElement.audioTracks. The individual tracks can be accessed using array syntax."]

properties.name: length
properties.overview: The number of tracks in the list.

properties.name: onaddtrack
properties.overview: An event handler to be called when the addtrack event is fired, indicating that a new audio track has been added to the media element.

properties.name: onchange
properties.overview: An event handler to be called when the change event occurs. This occurs when one or more tracks have been enabled or disabled by their enabled flag being changed.

properties.name: onremovetrack
properties.overview: An event handler to call when the removetrack event is sent, indicating that an audio track has been removed from the media element.

methods.name: getTrackById
methods.overview: Returns the AudioTrack found within the AudioTrackList whose id matches the specified string. If no match is found, null is returned.

parameters.name: id
parameters.overview: A DOMString indicating the ID of the track to locate within the track list.

name: Blob
overview: ["The Blob object represents a blob, which is a file-like object of immutable, raw data; they can be read as text or binary data, or converted into a ReadableStream so its methods can be used for processing the data.","Blobs can represent data that isn't necessarily in a JavaScript-native format. The File interface is based on Blob, inheriting blob functionality and expanding it to support files on the user's system."]

properties.name: size
properties.overview: The size, in bytes, of the data contained in the Blob object.

properties.name: type
properties.overview: A string indicating the MIME type of the data contained in the Blob. If the type is unknown, this string is empty.

methods.name: arrayBuffer
methods.overview: Returns a promise that resolves with an ArrayBuffer containing the entire contents of the Blob as binary data.

methods.name: slice
methods.overview: Returns a new Blob object containing the data in the specified range of bytes of the blob on which it's called.

parameters.name: start
parameters.overview: An index into the Blob indicating the first byte to include in the new Blob. If you specify a negative value, it's treated as an offset from the end of the Blob toward the beginning. For example, -10 would be the 10th from last byte in the Blob. The default value is 0. If you specify a value for start that is larger than the size of the source Blob, the returned Blob has size 0 and contains no data.

parameters.name: end
parameters.overview: An index into the Blob indicating the first byte that will *not* be included in the new Blob (i.e. the byte exactly at this index is not included). If you specify a negative value, it's treated as an offset from the end of the Blob toward the beginning. For example, -10 would be the 10th from last byte in the Blob. The default value is size.

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.overview: The content type to assign to the new Blob; this will be the value of its type property. The default value is an empty string.

methods.name: stream
methods.overview: Returns a ReadableStream that can be used to read the contents of the Blob.

methods.name: text
methods.overview: Returns a promise that resolves with a USVString containing the entire contents of the Blob interpreted as UTF-8 text.

name: Body
overview: ["The Body mixin of the Fetch API represents the body of the response/request, allowing you to declare what its content type is and how it should be handled.","Body is implemented by both Request and Response. This provides these objects with an associated body (a stream), a used flag (initially unset), and a MIME type (initially the empty byte sequence)."]

properties.name: body
properties.overview: A simple getter used to expose a ReadableStream of the body contents.

properties.name: bodyUsed
properties.overview: A Boolean that indicates whether the body has been read.

methods.name: arrayBuffer

methods.name: blob
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a Blob.

methods.name: formData

methods.name: json
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with the result of parsing the body text as JSON.

methods.name: text
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a USVString (text). The response is always decoded using UTF-8.

methods.name: replaceData
methods.overview: Replaces the specified amount of characters, starting at the specified offset, with the specified DOMString; when this method returns, data contains the modified DOMString.

methods.name: substringData
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the part of CharacterData.data of the specified length and starting at the specified offset.

methods.name: appendChild

If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. name: CSSRule
overview: ["The CSSRule interface represents a single CSS rule. There are several types of rules, listed in the Type constants section below.","The CSSRule interface specifies the properties common to all rules, while properties unique to specific rule types are specified in the more specialized interfaces for those rules' respective types.","References to a CSSRule may be obtained by looking at a CSSStyleSheet's cssRules list."]

properties.name: cssText
properties.overview: Represents the textual representation of the rule, e.g. "h1,h2 { font-size: 16pt }" or "@import 'url'". To access or modify parts of the rule (e.g. the value of "font-size" in the example) use the properties on the specialized interface for the rule's type.

properties.name: parentRule
properties.overview: Returns the containing rule, otherwise null. E.g. if this rule is a style rule inside an @media block, the parent rule would be that CSSMediaRule.

properties.name: parentStyleSheet
properties.overview: Returns the CSSStyleSheet object for the style sheet that contains this rule

properties.name: type
properties.overview: One of the Type constants indicating the type of CSS rule.

name: CSSRuleList
overview: ["A CSSRuleList is an (indirect-modify only) array-like object containing an ordered collection of CSSRule objects."]

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Returns the number of items in the collection.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: Returns the specific node at the given zero-based index into the list. Returns null if the index is out of range.

name: CSSStyleDeclaration
overview: ["The CSSStyleDeclaration interface represents an object that is a CSS declaration block, and exposes style information and various style-related methods and properties.","A CSSStyleDeclaration object can be exposed using three different APIs:"]

properties.name: cssFloat
properties.overview: The cssFloat attribute can be set for elements that generate boxes that are not absolutely positioned. The cssFloat attribute corresponds to the float Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) property. Getting this attribute is equivalent to calling the getProperty method. Setting this attribute is equivalent to calling the setProperty method.

properties.name: cssText
properties.overview: Textual representation of the declaration block. Setting this attribute changes the style.

properties.name: length
properties.overview: The number of properties. See the item() method below.

properties.name: parentRule
properties.overview: The containing CSSRule.

methods.name: getPropertyPriority
methods.overview: Returns the optional priority, "important".

parameters.name: property
parameters.overview: property is a DOMString representing the property name to be checked.

methods.name: getPropertyValue
methods.overview: Returns the property value given a property name.

parameters.name: property
parameters.overview: property is a DOMString representing the property name (hyphen case) to be checked.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: Returns a property name.

parameters.name: index
parameters.overview: index is the index of the node to be fetched. The index is zero-based.

methods.name: removeProperty
methods.overview: Removes a property from the CSS declaration block.

parameters.name: property
parameters.overview: property is a DOMString representing the property name to be removed. Note that multi-word property names are hyphenated and not camel-cased.

methods.name: setProperty
methods.overview: Modifies an existing CSS property or creates a new CSS property in the declaration block.

parameters.name: property
parameters.overview: propertyName is a DOMString representing the CSS property name (hyphen case) to be modified.

parameters.name: value
parameters.overview:
value Optional is a DOMString containing the new property value. If not specified, treated as the empty string.
  • Note: value must not contain "!important" -- that should be set using the priority parameter.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.overview:
priority Optional is a DOMString allowing the "important" CSS priority to be set. If not specified, treated as the empty string. The following values are accepted:
  • String value "important"
  • Keyword undefined
  • String empty value ""

properties.name: cssRules
properties.overview:
Returns a live CSSRuleList which maintains an up-to-date list of the CSSRule objects that comprise the stylesheet.

This is normally used to access individual rules like this:

styleSheet.cssRules[i] // where i = 0..cssRules.length-1

To add or remove items in cssRules, use the CSSStyleSheet's insertRule() and deleteRule() methods.

properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the location of the stylesheet.

parameters.overview:
A DOMString containing the rule to be inserted. What the inserted rule must contain depends on its type:

parameters.overview: A positive integer less than or equal to stylesheet.cssRules.length, representing the newly inserted rule's position in CSSStyleSheet.cssRules. The default is 0. (In older implementations, this was required. See Browser compatibility for details.)

properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the textual data contained in this object.

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Returns an unsigned long representing the size of the string contained in CharacterData.data.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

properties.name: nodeType
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned short representing the type of the node. Possible values are:
Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.name: nodeValue
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the value of the current node.

properties.name: ownerDocument
properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: previousSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the previous node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: textContent
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the textual content of an element and all its descendants.

properties.name: nextElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately following this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list following this node.

properties.name: previousElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately prior to this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list prior to this node.

methods.name: appendData
methods.overview: Appends the given DOMString to the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the concatenated DOMString.

methods.name: deleteData
methods.overview: Removes the specified amount of characters, starting at the specified offset, from the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the shortened DOMString.

methods.name: insertData
methods.overview: Inserts the specified characters, at the specified offset, in the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the modified DOMString.

methods.name: replaceData
methods.overview: Replaces the specified amount of characters, starting at the specified offset, with the specified DOMString; when this method returns, data contains the modified DOMString.

methods.name: substringData
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the part of CharacterData.data of the specified length and starting at the specified offset.

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: compareDocumentPosition
methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.name: other
parameters.overview: The other Node with which to compare the first node’s document position.

methods.name: contains
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not a node is a descendant of the calling node.

methods.name: getRootNode
methods.overview: Returns the context object's root which optionally includes the shadow root if it is available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
An object that sets options for getting the root node. The available options are:
  • composed: A Boolean that indicates whether the shadow root should be returned (false, the default), or a root node beyond shadow root (true).

methods.name: hasChildNodes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element has any child nodes.

methods.name: insertBefore
methods.overview: Inserts a Node before the reference node as a child of a specified parent node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to be inserted.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The node before which newNode is inserted. If this is null, then newNode is inserted at the end of parentNode's child nodes.

methods.name: isDefaultNamespace
methods.overview: Accepts a namespace URI as an argument and returns a Boolean with a value of true if the namespace is the default namespace on the given node or false if not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is a string representing the namespace against which the element will be checked.

methods.name: isEqualNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean which indicates whether or not two nodes are of the same type and all their defining data points match.

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode: The Node to compare equality with.

methods.name: isSameNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not the two nodes are the same (that is, they reference the same object).

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode The Node to test against.

methods.name: lookupNamespaceURI
methods.overview: Accepts a prefix and returns the namespace URI associated with it on the given node if found (and null if not). Supplying null for the prefix will return the default namespace.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.overview: The prefix to look for. If this parameter is null, the method will return the default namespace URI, if any.

methods.name: lookupPrefix
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the prefix for a given namespace URI, if present, and null if not. When multiple prefixes are possible, the result is implementation-dependent.

methods.name: normalize
methods.overview: Clean up all the text nodes under this element (merge adjacent, remove empty).

methods.name: removeChild
methods.overview: Removes a child node from the current element, which must be a child of the current node.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: child is the child node to be removed from the DOM.

methods.name: replaceChild
methods.overview: Replaces one child Node of the current one with the second one given in parameter.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The new node to replace oldChild. If it already exists in the DOM, it is first removed.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The child to be replaced.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.overview: Dispatches an event to this EventTarget.

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. Removal of a capturing listener does not affect a non-capturing version of the same listener, and vice versa.

methods.name: after
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just after this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: before
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just before this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: remove
methods.overview: Removes this ChildNode from the children list of its parent.

methods.name: replaceWith
methods.overview: Replaces this ChildNode in the children list of its parent with a set of Node or DOMString objects. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to replace.

name: DOMException
overview: ["The DOMException interface represents an abnormal event (called an exception) which occurs as a result of calling a method or accessing a property of a web API. This is basically how error conditions are described in web APIs.","Each exception has a name, which is a short \"CamelCase\" style string identifying the error or abnormal condition."]

properties.name: code
properties.overview: Returns a short that contains one of the error code constants, or 0 if none match. This field is used for historical reasons. New DOM exceptions don't use this anymore: they put this info in the DOMException.name attribute.

properties.name: message
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing a message or description associated with the given error name.

properties.name: name
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString that contains one of the strings associated with an error name.

name: DOMImplementation
overview: ["The DOMImplementation interface represents an object providing methods which are not dependent on any particular document. Such an object is returned by the Document.implementation property."]

methods.name: createDocument

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: Is a DOMString containing the qualified name, that is an optional prefix and colon plus the local root element name, of the document to be created.

parameters.name: doctype

methods.name: createDocumentType

parameters.name: systemId
parameters.overview: Is a DOMString containing the SYSTEM identifiers.

methods.name: createHTMLDocument
methods.overview: Creates and returns an HTML Document.

parameters.name: title
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing the title to give the new HTML document.

methods.name: hasFeature
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if a given feature is supported or not. This function is unreliable and kept for compatibility purpose alone: except for SVG-related queries, it always returns true. Old browsers are very inconsistent in their behavior.

name: DOMParser
overview: ["The DOMParser interface provides the ability to parse XML or HTML source code from a string into a DOM Document."]

methods.name: parseFromString
methods.overview: Parse XML from a string

name: DOMStringMap
overview: ["Used by the HTMLElement.dataset attribute to represent data for custom attributes added to elements."]

name: DOMTokenList
overview: ["The DOMTokenList interface represents a set of space-separated tokens. Such a set is returned by Element.classList, element and the current document.\">HTMLLinkElement.relList, element and the current document.\">HTMLAnchorElement.relList, element and the current document.\">HTMLAreaElement.relList, HTMLIframeElement.sandbox, or HTMLOutputElement.htmlFor. It is indexed beginning with 0 as with JavaScript Array objects. DOMTokenList is always case-sensitive."]

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Is an integer representing the number of objects stored in the object.

properties.name: value
properties.overview: A stringifier property that returns the value of the list as a DOMString.

methods.name: add
methods.overview: Adds the specified token(s) to the list.

parameters.name: tokens
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token (or tokens) to add to the tokenList.

methods.name: contains
methods.overview: Returns true if the list contains the given token, otherwise false.

parameters.name: token
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token you want to check for the existance of in the list.

methods.name: entries
methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing you to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object.

methods.name: forEach
methods.overview: Executes a provided callback function once per DOMTokenList element.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: Returns the item in the list by its index, or undefined if index is greater than or equal to the list's length.

parameters.name: index
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the index of the item you want to return.

methods.name: keys
methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object.

methods.name: remove
methods.overview: Removes the specified token(s) from the list.

parameters.name: tokens
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token you want to remove from the list. If the string is not in the list, no error is thrown, and nothing happens.

methods.name: replace
methods.overview: Replaces token with newToken.

parameters.name: token
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token you want to replace.

parameters.name: newToken
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token you want to replace oldToken with.

methods.name: supports
methods.overview: Returns true if a given token is in the associated attribute's supported tokens.

parameters.name: token
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing the token to query for.

methods.name: toggle
methods.overview: Removes token from the list if it exists, or adds token to the list if it doesn't. Returns a boolean indicating whether token is in the list after the operation.

parameters.name: token
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the token you want to toggle.

parameters.name: force
parameters.overview: A Boolean that, if included, turns the toggle into a one way-only operation. If set to false, then token will only be removed, but not added. If set to true, then token will only be added, but not removed.

methods.name: values
methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object.

name: Document
overview: ["The Document interface represents any web page loaded in the browser and serves as an entry point into the web page's content, which is the DOM tree. The DOM tree includes elements such as Element represents the content of an HTML document. There can be only one element in a document.\"><body> and element represents tabular data — that is, information presented in a two-dimensional table comprised of rows and columns of cells containing data.\"><table>, among many others. It provides functionality globally to the document, like how to obtain the page's URL and create new elements in the document."]

properties.name: anchors

properties.name: body
properties.overview: Returns the <body> or <frameset> node of the current document.

properties.name: characterSet

properties.name: compatMode

properties.name: contentType

properties.name: cookie

properties.name: documentElement
properties.overview: Returns the Element that is a direct child of the document. For HTML documents, this is normally the HTMLHtmlElement object representing the document's <html> element.

properties.name: documentURI
properties.overview: Returns the document location as a string.

properties.name: domain
properties.overview: Gets/sets the domain of the current document.

properties.name: embeds
properties.overview: Returns a list of the embedded <embed> elements within the current document.

properties.name: featurePolicy
properties.overview: Returns the FeaturePolicy interface which provides a simple API for introspecting the feature policies applied to a specific document.

properties.name: fonts
properties.overview: Returns the FontFaceSet interface of the current document.

properties.name: forms
properties.overview: Returns a list of the <form> elements within the current document.

properties.name: fullscreenEnabled
properties.overview: Indicates whether or not full-screen mode is available.

properties.name: head
properties.overview: Returns the <head> element of the current document.

properties.name: hidden
properties.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating if the page is considered hidden or not.

properties.name: images

properties.name: implementation

properties.name: lastModified

properties.name: links

properties.name: location
properties.overview: Returns the URI of the current document.

properties.name: onfullscreenerror

properties.name: onpointerlockerror

properties.name: onvisibilitychange

properties.name: plugins

properties.name: readyState

properties.name: referrer

methods.name: createNodeIterator
methods.overview: Creates a NodeIterator object.

parameters.name: root
parameters.overview: The root node at which to begin the NodeIterator's traversal.

parameters.name: whatToShow
parameters.overview:
Is an optional unsigned long representing a bitmask created by combining the constant properties of NodeFilter. It is a convenient way of filtering for certain types of node. It defaults to 0xFFFFFFFF representing the SHOW_ALL constant.
Constant Numerical value Description
NodeFilter.SHOW_ALL -1 (that is the max value of unsigned long) Shows all nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ATTRIBUTE 2

Shows attribute Attr nodes.

This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with an Attr node as its root. In this case, it means that the attribute node will appear in the first position of the iteration or traversal. Since attributes are never children of other nodes, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_CDATA_SECTION 8 Shows CDATASection nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_COMMENT 128 Shows Comment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT 256 Shows Document nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT 1024 Shows DocumentFragment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_TYPE 512 Shows DocumentType nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT 1 Shows Element nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY 32 Shows Entity nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with an Entity node as its root; in this case, it means that the Entity node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY_REFERENCE 16 Shows EntityReference nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_NOTATION 2048 Shows Notation nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a TreeWalker with a Notation node as its root; in this case, it means that the Notation node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION 64 Shows ProcessingInstruction nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT 4 Shows Text nodes.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.overview: An object implementing the NodeFilter interface. Its acceptNode() method will be called for each node in the subtree based at root which is accepted as included by the whatToShow flag to determine whether or not to include it in the list of iterable nodes (a simple callback function may also be used instead). The method should return one of NodeFilter.FILTER_ACCEPT, NodeFilter.FILTER_REJECT, or NodeFilter.FILTER_SKIP. See the Example.

methods.name: importNode
methods.overview: Returns a clone of a node from an external document.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The external Node or DocumentFragment to import into the current document.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
A Boolean which controls whether to include the entire DOM subtree of the externalNode in the import.
  • If deep is set to true, then externalNode and all of its descendants are copied.
  • If deep is set to false, then only externalNode is imported — the new node has no children.

Note: In the DOM4 specification, deep was an optional argument with a default value of true.

This default has changed in the latest spec! The new default value is false.

Best Practice: Though it's still an optional argument, you should always provide the deep argument for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3), the console warns developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent

parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. Removal of a capturing listener does not affect a non-capturing version of the same listener, and vice versa.

parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault().
