parameters.overview: nodeName is a string specifying the name of the attribute.

methods.name: getAttributeNS
methods.overview: Retrieves the value of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node and returns it as an Object.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: The namespace in which to look for the specified attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: The name of the attribute to look for.

methods.name: getBoundingClientRect
methods.overview: Returns the size of an element and its position relative to the viewport.

methods.name: getClientRects
methods.overview: Returns a collection of rectangles that indicate the bounding rectangles for each line of text in a client.

methods.name: getElementsByClassName
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection that contains all descendants of the current element that possess the list of classes given in the parameter.

parameters.name: classNames
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more class names to match on, separated by whitespace.

methods.name: getElementsByTagName
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all descendant elements, of a particular tag name, from the current element.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: tagName is the qualified name to look for. The special string "*" represents all elements. For compatibility with XHTML, lower-case should be used.

methods.name: getElementsByTagNameNS
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all descendant elements, of a particular tag name and namespace, from the current element.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is the namespace URI of elements to look for (see Element.namespaceURI and Attr.namespaceURI). For example, if you need to look for XHTML elements, use the XHTML namespace URI, http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: localName is either the local name of elements to look for or the special value "*", which matches all elements (see Element.localName and Attr.localName).

methods.name: hasAttribute
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has the specified attribute or not.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: is a string representing the name of the attribute.

methods.name: hasAttributeNS
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has the specified attribute, in the specified namespace, or not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string specifying the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: localName is the name of the attribute.

methods.name: hasAttributes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has one or more HTML attributes present.

methods.name: hasPointerCapture
methods.overview: Indicates whether the element on which it is invoked has pointer capture for the pointer identified by the given pointer ID.

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: insertAdjacentElement
methods.overview: Inserts a given element node at a given position relative to the element it is invoked upon.

parameters.name: where
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the targetElement; must match (case-insensitively) one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the targetElement itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the targetElement, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the targetElement, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the targetElement itself.

parameters.name: element
parameters.overview: The element to be inserted into the tree.

methods.name: insertAdjacentHTML
methods.overview: Parses the text as HTML or XML and inserts the resulting nodes into the tree in the position given.

parameters.name: position
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the element; must be one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the element itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the element, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the element, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the element itself.

parameters.name: text
parameters.overview: The string to be parsed as HTML or XML and inserted into the tree.

methods.name: insertAdjacentText
methods.overview: Inserts a given text node at a given position relative to the element it is invoked upon.

parameters.name: where
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the element; must be one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the element itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the element, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the element, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the element itself.

parameters.name: data
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the text to be inserted into the tree.

methods.name: matches
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element would be selected by the specified selector string.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: selectorString is a string representing the selector to test.

methods.name: releasePointerCapture
methods.overview: Releases (stops) pointer capture that was previously set for a specific pointer event.

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.overview: Removes the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute to remove from the element. If the specified attribute does not exist, removeAttribute() returns without generating an error.

methods.name: removeAttributeNode
methods.overview: Removes the node representation of the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attributeNode is the Attr node that needs to be removed.

methods.name: removeAttributeNS
methods.overview: Removes the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string that contains the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: attrName is a string that names the attribute to be removed from the current node.

methods.name: requestFullscreen
methods.overview: Asynchronously asks the browser to make the element full-screen.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview: A FullscreenOptions object  providing options that control the behavior of the transition to full-screen mode. Currently, the only option is navigationUI, which controls whether or not to show navigation UI while the element is in full-screen mode. The default value is "auto", which indicates that the browser should decide what to do.

methods.name: requestPointerLock
methods.overview: Allows to asynchronously ask for the pointer to be locked on the given element.

methods.name: scroll
methods.overview: Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates inside a given element.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: The pixel along the horizontal axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: The pixel along the vertical axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

methods.name: scrollBy
methods.overview: Scrolls an element by the given amount.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: x-coord is the horizontal pixel value that you want to scroll by.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: y-coord is the vertical pixel value that you want to scroll by.

methods.name: scrollIntoView
methods.overview: Scrolls the page until the element gets into the view.

parameters.name: arg
parameters.overview:
• Is a Boolean value:
    • If true, the top of the element will be aligned to the top of the visible area of the scrollable ancestor. Corresponds to scrollIntoViewOptions: {block: "start", inline: "nearest"}. This is the default value.
    • If false, the bottom of the element will be aligned to the bottom of the visible area of the scrollable ancestor. Corresponds to scrollIntoViewOptions: {block: "end", inline: "nearest"}.
  • Is an Object with the following properties:
    behavior Optional
    Defines the transition animation.
    One of auto or smooth. Defaults to auto.
    block Optional
    Defines vertical alignment.
    One of start, center, end, or nearest. Defaults to start.
    inline Optional
    Defines horizontal alignment.
    One of start, center, end, or nearest. Defaults to nearest.

methods.name: scrollTo
methods.overview: Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates inside a given element.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: x-coord is the pixel along the horizontal axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: y-coord is the pixel along the vertical axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.overview: Sets the value of a named attribute of the current node.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute whose value is to be set. The attribute name is automatically converted to all lower-case when setAttribute() is called on an HTML element in an HTML document.

parameters.name: value
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing the value to assign to the attribute. Any non-string value specified is converted automatically into a string.

methods.name: setAttributeNode
methods.overview: Sets the node representation of the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attribute is the Attr node to set on the element.

methods.name: setAttributeNodeNS
methods.overview: Sets the node representation of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attributeNode is an Attr node.

methods.name: setAttributeNS
methods.overview: Sets the value of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string specifying the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: name is a string identifying the attribute by its qualified name; that is, a namespace prefix followed by a colon followed by a local name.

parameters.name: value
parameters.overview: value is the desired string value of the new attribute.

methods.name: setPointerCapture
methods.overview: Designates a specific element as the capture target of future pointer events.

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: toggleAttribute
methods.overview: Toggles a boolean attribute, removing it if it is present and adding it if it is not present, on the specified element.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute to be toggled. The attribute name is automatically converted to all lower-case when toggleAttribute() is called on an HTML element in an HTML document.

parameters.name: force
parameters.overview: A boolean value to determine whether the attribute should be added or removed, no matter whether the attribute is present or not at the moment.

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: compareDocumentPosition
methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.name: other
parameters.overview: The other Node with which to compare the first node’s document position.

methods.name: contains
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not a node is a descendant of the calling node.

methods.name: getRootNode
methods.overview: Returns the context object's root which optionally includes the shadow root if it is available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
An object that sets options for getting the root node. The available options are:
  • composed: A Boolean that indicates whether the shadow root should be returned (false, the default), or a root node beyond shadow root (true).

methods.name: hasChildNodes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element has any child nodes.

methods.name: insertBefore
methods.overview: Inserts a Node before the reference node as a child of a specified parent node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to be inserted.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The node before which newNode is inserted. If this is null, then newNode is inserted at the end of parentNode's child nodes.

methods.name: isDefaultNamespace
methods.overview: Accepts a namespace URI as an argument and returns a Boolean with a value of true if the namespace is the default namespace on the given node or false if not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is a string representing the namespace against which the element will be checked.

methods.name: isEqualNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean which indicates whether or not two nodes are of the same type and all their defining data points match.

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode: The Node to compare equality with.

methods.name: isSameNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not the two nodes are the same (that is, they reference the same object).

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode The Node to test against.

methods.name: lookupNamespaceURI
methods.overview: Accepts a prefix and returns the namespace URI associated with it on the given node if found (and null if not). Supplying null for the prefix will return the default namespace.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.overview: The prefix to look for. If this parameter is null, the method will return the default namespace URI, if any.

methods.name: lookupPrefix
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the prefix for a given namespace URI, if present, and null if not. When multiple prefixes are possible, the result is implementation-dependent.

methods.name: normalize
methods.overview: Clean up all the text nodes under this element (merge adjacent, remove empty).

methods.name: removeChild
methods.overview: Removes a child node from the current element, which must be a child of the current node.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: child is the child node to be removed from the DOM.

methods.name: replaceChild
methods.overview: Replaces one child Node of the current one with the second one given in parameter.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The new node to replace oldChild. If it already exists in the DOM, it is first removed.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The child to be replaced.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.overview: Dispatches an event to this EventTarget.

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. Removal of a capturing listener does not affect a non-capturing version of the same listener, and vice versa.

methods.name: after
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just after this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: before
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just before this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: remove
methods.overview: Removes this ChildNode from the children list of its parent.

methods.name: replaceWith
methods.overview: Replaces this ChildNode in the children list of its parent with a set of Node or DOMString objects. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to replace.

methods.name: append
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects after the last child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: prepend
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects before the first child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: One or more nodes to insert before the first child node currently in the ParentNode. Each node can be specified as either a Node object or as a string; strings are inserted as new Text nodes.

methods.name: querySelector
methods.overview: Returns the first Element with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid compound selector list supported by the browser; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

methods.name: querySelectorAll
methods.overview: Returns a NodeList representing a list of elements with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid CSS selector string; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

name: HTMLEmbedElement
overview: ["The HTMLEmbedElement interface provides special properties (beyond the regular HTMLElement interface it also has available to it by inheritance) for manipulating element embeds external content at the specified point in the document. This content is provided by an external application or other source of interactive content such as a browser plug-in.\"><embed> elements."]

properties.name: align
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing an enumerated property indicating alignment of the element's contents with respect to the surrounding context. The possible values are "left", "right", "center", and "justify".

properties.name: height
properties.overview: Is a DOMString reflecting the height HTML attribute, containing the displayed height of the resource.

properties.name: name
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the name of the embedded object.

properties.name: src
properties.overview: Is a DOMString that reflects the src HTML attribute, containing the address of the resource.

properties.name: type
properties.overview: Is a DOMString that reflects the type HTML attribute, containing the type of the resource.

properties.name: width
properties.overview: Is a DOMString that reflects the width HTML attribute, containing the displayed width of the resource.

properties.name: accessKey
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the access key assigned to the element.

properties.name: dir
properties.overview: Is a DOMString, reflecting the dir global attribute, representing the directionality of the element. Possible values are "ltr", "rtl", and "auto".

properties.name: draggable
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating if the element can be dragged.

properties.name: hidden
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating if the element is hidden or not.

properties.name: inert
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating whether the user agent must act as though the given node is absent for the purposes of user interaction events, in-page text searches ("find in page"), and text selection.

properties.name: innerText
properties.overview: Represents the "rendered" text content of a node and its descendants. As a getter, it approximates the text the user would get if they highlighted the contents of the element with the cursor and then copied it to the clipboard.

properties.name: lang
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the language of an element's attributes, text, and element contents.

properties.name: offsetHeight
properties.overview: Returns a double containing the height of an element, relative to the layout.

properties.name: offsetLeft
properties.overview: Returns a double, the distance from this element's left border to its offsetParent's left border.

properties.name: offsetParent
properties.overview: Returns a Element that is the element from which all offset calculations are currently computed.

properties.name: offsetTop
properties.overview: Returns a double, the distance from this element's top border to its offsetParent's top border.

properties.name: offsetWidth
properties.overview: Returns a double containing the width of an element, relative to the layout.

properties.name: spellcheck
properties.overview: Is a Boolean that controls spell-checking. It is present on all HTML elements, though it doesn't have an effect on all of them.

properties.name: title
properties.overview: Is a DOMString containing the text that appears in a popup box when mouse is over the element.

properties.name: translate
properties.overview: Is a Boolean representing the translation.

properties.name: attributes
properties.overview: Returns a NamedNodeMap object containing the assigned attributes of the corresponding HTML element.

properties.name: classList
properties.overview: Returns a DOMTokenList containing the list of class attributes.

properties.name: className
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the class of the element.

properties.name: clientHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner height of the element.

properties.name: clientLeft
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the left border of the element.

properties.name: clientTop
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the top border of the element.

properties.name: clientWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner width of the element.

properties.name: id
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the id of the element.

properties.name: innerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element's content.

properties.name: localName
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the local part of the qualified name of the element.

properties.name: namespaceURI
properties.overview:
The namespace URI of the element, or null if it is no namespace.

Note: In Firefox 3.5 and earlier, HTML elements are in no namespace. In later versions, HTML elements are in the http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml namespace in both HTML and XML trees.

properties.name: onfullscreenchange
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenchange event, which is sent when the element enters or exits full-screen mode. This can be used to watch both for successful expected transitions, but also to watch for unexpected changes, such as when your app is running in the background.

properties.name: onfullscreenerror
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenerror event, which is sent when an error occurs while attempting to change into full-screen mode.

properties.name: outerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element including its content. When used as a setter, replaces the element with nodes parsed from the given string.

properties.name: part
properties.overview: Represents the part identifier(s) of the element (i.e. set using the part attribute), returned as a DOMTokenList.

properties.name: prefix
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the namespace prefix of the element, or null if no prefix is specified.

properties.name: scrollHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view height of an element.

properties.name: scrollLeft
properties.overview: Is a Number representing the left scroll offset of the element.

properties.name: scrollTop
properties.overview: A Number representing number of pixels the top of the document is scrolled vertically.

properties.name: scrollWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view width of the element.

properties.name: shadowRoot
properties.overview: Returns the open shadow root that is hosted by the element, or null if no open shadow root is present.

properties.name: slot
properties.overview: Returns the name of the shadow DOM slot the element is inserted in.

properties.name: tagName
properties.overview: Returns a String with the name of the tag for the given element.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

properties.name: nodeType
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned short representing the type of the node. Possible values are:
Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.name: nodeValue
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the value of the current node.

properties.name: ownerDocument
properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: previousSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the previous node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: textContent
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the textual content of an element and all its descendants.

properties.name: style
properties.overview: The style property is used to get as well as set the inline style of an element. When getting, it returns a CSSStyleDeclaration object that contains a list of all styles properties for that element with values assigned for the attributes that are defined in the element's inline style attribute.

properties.name: onabort
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the abort event is raised.

properties.name: onanimationend
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationend event is sent, indicating that a CSS animation has stopped playing.

properties.name: onanimationiteration
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationiteration event has been sent, indicating that a CSS animation has begun playing a new iteration of the animation sequence.

properties.name: onanimationstart
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationstart event is sent, indicating that a CSS animation has started playing.

properties.name: onauxclick
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an auxclick event is sent, indicating that a non-primary button has been pressed on an input device (e.g. a middle mouse button).

properties.name: onblur
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the blur event is raised.

properties.name: oncancel
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the cancel event is raised.

properties.name: oncanplay
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the canplay event is raised.

properties.name: oncanplaythrough

properties.name: nextElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately following this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list following this node.

properties.name: previousElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately prior to this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list prior to this node.

properties.name: childElementCount
properties.overview: Returns the number of children of this ParentNode which are elements.

properties.name: children
properties.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all of the Element objects that are children of this ParentNode, omitting all of its non-element nodes.

properties.name: firstElementChild
properties.overview: Returns the first node which is both a child of this ParentNode and is also an Element, or null if there is none.

properties.name: lastElementChild
properties.overview: Returns the last node which is both a child of this ParentNode and is an Element, or null if there is none.

properties.name: assignedSlot

methods.name: click
methods.overview: Sends a mouse click event to the element.

methods.name: attachShadow
methods.overview: Attaches a shadow DOM tree to the specified element and returns a reference to its ShadowRoot.

parameters.name: init
parameters.overview:
A ShadowRootInit dictionary, which can contain the following fields:
mode

A string specifying the encapsulation mode for the shadow DOM tree. This can be one of:

  • open: Elements of the shadow root are accessible from JavaScript outside the root, for example using Element.shadowRoot:
      
    element.shadowRoot; // Returns a ShadowRoot obj
  • closed: Denies access to the node(s) of a closed shadow root from JavaScript outside it:
      
    element.shadowRoot; // Returns null
delegatesFocus
A boolean that, when set to true, specifies behavior that mitigates custom element issues around focusability. When a non-focusable part of the shadow DOM is clicked, the first focusable part is given focus, and the shadow host is given any available :focus styling.

methods.name: closest
methods.overview: Returns the Element which is the closest ancestor of the current element (or the current element itself) which matches the selectors given in parameter.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview:
selectors is a DOMString containing a selector list.
ex: p:hover, .toto + q

methods.name: computedStyleMap
methods.overview: Returns a StylePropertyMapReadOnly interface which provides a read-only representation of a CSS declaration block that is an alternative to CSSStyleDeclaration.

methods.name: getAttribute
methods.overview: Retrieves the value of the named attribute from the current node and returns it as an Object.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: attributeName is the name of the attribute whose value you want to get.

methods.name: getAttributeNames
methods.overview: Returns an array of attribute names from the current element.

methods.name: getAttributeNode
methods.overview: Retrieves the node representation of the named attribute from the current node and returns it as an Attr.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: attrName is a string containing the name of the attribute.

methods.name: getAttributeNodeNS
methods.overview: Retrieves the node representation of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node and returns it as an Attr.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string specifying the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: nodeName is a string specifying the name of the attribute.

methods.name: getAttributeNS
methods.overview: Retrieves the value of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node and returns it as an Object.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: The namespace in which to look for the specified attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: The name of the attribute to look for.

methods.name: getBoundingClientRect
methods.overview: Returns the size of an element and its position relative to the viewport.

methods.name: getClientRects
methods.overview: Returns a collection of rectangles that indicate the bounding rectangles for each line of text in a client.

methods.name: getElementsByClassName
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection that contains all descendants of the current element that possess the list of classes given in the parameter.

parameters.name: classNames
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more class names to match on, separated by whitespace.

methods.name: getElementsByTagName
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all descendant elements, of a particular tag name, from the current element.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: tagName is the qualified name to look for. The special string "*" represents all elements. For compatibility with XHTML, lower-case should be used.

methods.name: getElementsByTagNameNS
methods.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all descendant elements, of a particular tag name and namespace, from the current element.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is the namespace URI of elements to look for (see Element.namespaceURI and Attr.namespaceURI). For example, if you need to look for XHTML elements, use the XHTML namespace URI, http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: localName is either the local name of elements to look for or the special value "*", which matches all elements (see Element.localName and Attr.localName).

methods.name: hasAttribute
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has the specified attribute or not.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: is a string representing the name of the attribute.

methods.name: hasAttributeNS
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has the specified attribute, in the specified namespace, or not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string specifying the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: localName is the name of the attribute.

methods.name: hasAttributes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating if the element has one or more HTML attributes present.

methods.name: hasPointerCapture
methods.overview: Indicates whether the element on which it is invoked has pointer capture for the pointer identified by the given pointer ID.

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: insertAdjacentElement
methods.overview: Inserts a given element node at a given position relative to the element it is invoked upon.

parameters.name: where
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the targetElement; must match (case-insensitively) one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the targetElement itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the targetElement, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the targetElement, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the targetElement itself.

parameters.name: element
parameters.overview: The element to be inserted into the tree.

methods.name: insertAdjacentHTML
methods.overview: Parses the text as HTML or XML and inserts the resulting nodes into the tree in the position given.

parameters.name: position
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the element; must be one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the element itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the element, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the element, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the element itself.

parameters.name: text
parameters.overview: The string to be parsed as HTML or XML and inserted into the tree.

methods.name: insertAdjacentText
methods.overview: Inserts a given text node at a given position relative to the element it is invoked upon.

parameters.name: where
parameters.overview:
A DOMString representing the position relative to the element; must be one of the following strings:
  • 'beforebegin': Before the element itself.
  • 'afterbegin': Just inside the element, before its first child.
  • 'beforeend': Just inside the element, after its last child.
  • 'afterend': After the element itself.

parameters.name: data
parameters.overview: A DOMString representing the text to be inserted into the tree.

methods.name: matches
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element would be selected by the specified selector string.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: selectorString is a string representing the selector to test.

methods.name: releasePointerCapture

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.overview: Removes the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute to remove from the element. If the specified attribute does not exist, removeAttribute() returns without generating an error.

methods.name: removeAttributeNode
methods.overview: Removes the node representation of the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attributeNode is the Attr node that needs to be removed.

methods.name: removeAttributeNS
methods.overview: Removes the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string that contains the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: localName
parameters.overview: attrName is a string that names the attribute to be removed from the current node.

methods.name: requestFullscreen
methods.overview: Asynchronously asks the browser to make the element full-screen.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview: A FullscreenOptions object  providing options that control the behavior of the transition to full-screen mode. Currently, the only option is navigationUI, which controls whether or not to show navigation UI while the element is in full-screen mode. The default value is "auto", which indicates that the browser should decide what to do.

methods.name: requestPointerLock
methods.overview: Allows to asynchronously ask for the pointer to be locked on the given element.

methods.name: scroll
methods.overview: Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates inside a given element.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: The pixel along the horizontal axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: The pixel along the vertical axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

methods.name: scrollBy
methods.overview: Scrolls an element by the given amount.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: x-coord is the horizontal pixel value that you want to scroll by.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: y-coord is the vertical pixel value that you want to scroll by.

methods.name: scrollIntoView
methods.overview: Scrolls the page until the element gets into the view.

parameters.name: arg
parameters.overview:
• Is a Boolean value:
    • If true, the top of the element will be aligned to the top of the visible area of the scrollable ancestor. Corresponds to scrollIntoViewOptions: {block: "start", inline: "nearest"}. This is the default value.
    • If false, the bottom of the element will be aligned to the bottom of the visible area of the scrollable ancestor. Corresponds to scrollIntoViewOptions: {block: "end", inline: "nearest"}.
  • Is an Object with the following properties:
    behavior Optional
    Defines the transition animation.
    One of auto or smooth. Defaults to auto.
    block Optional
    Defines vertical alignment.
    One of start, center, end, or nearest. Defaults to start.
    inline Optional
    Defines horizontal alignment.
    One of start, center, end, or nearest. Defaults to nearest.

methods.name: scrollTo
methods.overview: Scrolls to a particular set of coordinates inside a given element.

parameters.name: x
parameters.overview: x-coord is the pixel along the horizontal axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

parameters.name: y
parameters.overview: y-coord is the pixel along the vertical axis of the element that you want displayed in the upper left.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.overview: Sets the value of a named attribute of the current node.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute whose value is to be set. The attribute name is automatically converted to all lower-case when setAttribute() is called on an HTML element in an HTML document.

parameters.name: value
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing the value to assign to the attribute. Any non-string value specified is converted automatically into a string.

methods.name: setAttributeNode
methods.overview: Sets the node representation of the named attribute from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attribute is the Attr node to set on the element.

methods.name: setAttributeNodeNS
methods.overview: Sets the node representation of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.overview: attributeNode is an Attr node.

methods.name: setAttributeNS
methods.overview: Sets the value of the attribute with the specified name and namespace, from the current node.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespace is a string specifying the namespace of the attribute.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: name is a string identifying the attribute by its qualified name; that is, a namespace prefix followed by a colon followed by a local name.

parameters.name: value
parameters.overview: value is the desired string value of the new attribute.

methods.name: setPointerCapture
methods.overview: Designates a specific element as the capture target of future pointer events.

parameters.name: pointerId
parameters.overview: The pointerId of a PointerEvent object.

methods.name: toggleAttribute
methods.overview: Toggles a boolean attribute, removing it if it is present and adding it if it is not present, on the specified element.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: A DOMString specifying the name of the attribute to be toggled. The attribute name is automatically converted to all lower-case when toggleAttribute() is called on an HTML element in an HTML document.

parameters.name: force
parameters.overview: A boolean value to determine whether the attribute should be added or removed, no matter whether the attribute is present or not at the moment.

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: compareDocumentPosition
methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.name: other
parameters.overview: The other Node with which to compare the first node’s document position.

methods.name: contains
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not a node is a descendant of the calling node.

methods.name: getRootNode
methods.overview: Returns the context object's root which optionally includes the shadow root if it is available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
An object that sets options for getting the root node. The available options are:
  • composed: A Boolean that indicates whether the shadow root should be returned (false, the default), or a root node beyond shadow root (true).

methods.name: hasChildNodes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element has any child nodes.

methods.name: insertBefore
methods.overview: Inserts a Node before the reference node as a child of a specified parent node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to be inserted.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The node before which newNode is inserted. If this is null, then newNode is inserted at the end of parentNode's child nodes.

methods.name: isDefaultNamespace
methods.overview: Accepts a namespace URI as an argument and returns a Boolean with a value of true if the namespace is the default namespace on the given node or false if not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is a string representing the namespace against which the element will be checked.

methods.name: isEqualNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean which indicates whether or not two nodes are of the same type and all their defining data points match.

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode: The Node to compare equality with.

methods.name: isSameNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not the two nodes are the same (that is, they reference the same object).

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode The Node to test against.

methods.name: lookupNamespaceURI
methods.overview: Accepts a prefix and returns the namespace URI associated with it on the given node if found (and null if not). Supplying null for the prefix will return the default namespace.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.overview: The prefix to look for. If this parameter is null, the method will return the default namespace URI, if any.

methods.name: lookupPrefix
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the prefix for a given namespace URI, if present, and null if not. When multiple prefixes are possible, the result is implementation-dependent.

methods.name: normalize
methods.overview: Clean up all the text nodes under this element (merge adjacent, remove empty).

methods.name: removeChild
methods.overview: Removes a child node from the current element, which must be a child of the current node.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: child is the child node to be removed from the DOM.

methods.name: replaceChild
methods.overview: Replaces one child Node of the current one with the second one given in parameter.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The new node to replace oldChild. If it already exists in the DOM, it is first removed.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The child to be replaced.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.overview: Dispatches an event to this EventTarget.

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. Removal of a capturing listener does not affect a non-capturing version of the same listener, and vice versa.

methods.name: after
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just after this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: before
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just before this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: remove
methods.overview: Removes this ChildNode from the children list of its parent.

methods.name: replaceWith
methods.overview: Replaces this ChildNode in the children list of its parent with a set of Node or DOMString objects. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to replace.

methods.name: append
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects after the last child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: prepend
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects before the first child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: One or more nodes to insert before the first child node currently in the ParentNode. Each node can be specified as either a Node object or as a string; strings are inserted as new Text nodes.

methods.name: querySelector
methods.overview: Returns the first Element with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid compound selector list supported by the browser; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

methods.name: querySelectorAll
methods.overview: Returns a NodeList representing a list of elements with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid CSS selector string; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

name: HTMLFieldSetElement
overview: ["The HTMLFieldSetElement interface provides special properties and methods (beyond the regular HTMLElement interface it also has available to it by inheritance) for manipulating the layout and presentation of element is used to group several controls as well as labels ( elements."]

properties.name: disabled
properties.overview: A Boolean reflecting the disabled HTML attribute, indicating whether the user can interact with the control.

properties.name: elements
properties.overview: The elements belonging to this field set. The type of this property depends on the version of the spec that is implemented by the browser.

properties.name: form
properties.overview:
An HTMLFormControlsCollection or HTMLCollection referencing the containing form element, if this element is in a form.
If the field set is not a descendant of a form element, then the attribute can be the ID of any form element in the same document it is related to, or the null value if none matches.

properties.name: name
properties.overview: A DOMString reflecting the name HTML attribute, containing the name of the field set, used for submitting the form.

properties.name: type
properties.overview: The DOMString "fieldset".

properties.name: validationMessage
properties.overview: A DOMString representing a localized message that describes the validation constraints that the element does not satisfy (if any). This is the empty string if the element is not a candidate for constraint validation (willValidate is false), or it satisfies its constraints.

properties.name: validity
properties.overview: A ValidityState representing the validity states that this element is in.

properties.name: willValidate
properties.overview: A Boolean false, because <fieldset> objects are never candidates for constraint validation.

properties.name: accessKey
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the access key assigned to the element.

properties.name: dir
properties.overview: Is a DOMString, reflecting the dir global attribute, representing the directionality of the element. Possible values are "ltr", "rtl", and "auto".

properties.name: draggable
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating if the element can be dragged.

properties.name: hidden
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating if the element is hidden or not.

properties.name: inert
properties.overview: Is a Boolean indicating whether the user agent must act as though the given node is absent for the purposes of user interaction events, in-page text searches ("find in page"), and text selection.

properties.name: innerText
properties.overview: Represents the "rendered" text content of a node and its descendants. As a getter, it approximates the text the user would get if they highlighted the contents of the element with the cursor and then copied it to the clipboard.

properties.name: lang
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the language of an element's attributes, text, and element contents.

properties.name: offsetHeight
properties.overview: Returns a double containing the height of an element, relative to the layout.

properties.name: offsetLeft
properties.overview: Returns a double, the distance from this element's left border to its offsetParent's left border.

properties.name: offsetParent
properties.overview: Returns a Element that is the element from which all offset calculations are currently computed.

properties.name: offsetTop
properties.overview: Returns a double, the distance from this element's top border to its offsetParent's top border.

properties.name: offsetWidth
properties.overview: Returns a double containing the width of an element, relative to the layout.

properties.name: spellcheck
properties.overview: Is a Boolean that controls spell-checking. It is present on all HTML elements, though it doesn't have an effect on all of them.

properties.name: title
properties.overview: Is a DOMString containing the text that appears in a popup box when mouse is over the element.

properties.name: translate
properties.overview: Is a Boolean representing the translation.

properties.name: attributes
properties.overview: Returns a NamedNodeMap object containing the assigned attributes of the corresponding HTML element.

properties.name: classList
properties.overview: Returns a DOMTokenList containing the list of class attributes.

properties.name: className
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the class of the element.

properties.name: clientHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner height of the element.

properties.name: clientLeft
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the left border of the element.

properties.name: clientTop
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the top border of the element.

properties.name: clientWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner width of the element.

properties.name: id
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the id of the element.

properties.name: innerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element's content.

properties.name: localName
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the local part of the qualified name of the element.

properties.name: namespaceURI
properties.overview:
The namespace URI of the element, or null if it is no namespace.

Note: In Firefox 3.5 and earlier, HTML elements are in no namespace. In later versions, HTML elements are in the http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml namespace in both HTML and XML trees.

properties.name: onfullscreenchange
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenchange event, which is sent when the element enters or exits full-screen mode. This can be used to watch both for successful expected transitions, but also to watch for unexpected changes, such as when your app is running in the background.

properties.name: onfullscreenerror
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenerror event, which is sent when an error occurs while attempting to change into full-screen mode.

properties.name: outerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element including its content. When used as a setter, replaces the element with nodes parsed from the given string.

properties.name: part
properties.overview: Represents the part identifier(s) of the element (i.e. set using the part attribute), returned as a DOMTokenList.

properties.name: prefix
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the namespace prefix of the element, or null if no prefix is specified.

properties.name: scrollHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view height of an element.

properties.name: scrollLeft
properties.overview: Is a Number representing the left scroll offset of the element.

properties.name: scrollTop
properties.overview: A Number representing number of pixels the top of the document is scrolled vertically.

properties.name: scrollWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view width of the element.

properties.name: shadowRoot
properties.overview: Returns the open shadow root that is hosted by the element, or null if no open shadow root is present.

properties.name: slot
properties.overview: Returns the name of the shadow DOM slot the element is inserted in.

properties.name: tagName
properties.overview: Returns a String with the name of the tag for the given element.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

properties.name: nodeType
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned short representing the type of the node. Possible values are:
Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.name: nodeValue
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the value of the current node.

properties.name: ownerDocument
properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: previousSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the previous node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: textContent
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the textual content of an element and all its descendants.

properties.name: style
properties.overview: The style property is used to get as well as set the inline style of an element. When getting, it returns a CSSStyleDeclaration object that contains a list of all styles properties for that element with values assigned for the attributes that are defined in the element's inline style attribute.

properties.name: onabort
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the abort event is raised.

properties.name: onanimationend
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationend event is sent, indicating that a CSS animation has stopped playing.

properties.name: onanimationiteration
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationiteration event has been sent, indicating that a CSS animation has begun playing a new iteration of the animation sequence.

properties.name: onanimationstart
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an animationstart event is sent, indicating that a CSS animation has started playing.

properties.name: onauxclick
properties.overview: An EventHandler called when an auxclick event is sent, indicating that a non-primary button has been pressed on an input device (e.g. a middle mouse button).

properties.overview: Is an EventHandler representing the code to be called when the focus event is raised.

properties.name: onformdata
properties.overview: Is an EventHandler for processing formdata events, fired after the entry list representing the form's data is constructed.

properties.name: ongotpointercapture

properties.name: onlostpointercapture
