overview: ["The Location interface represents the location (URL) of the object it is linked to. Changes done on it are reflected on the object it relates to. Both the Document and Window interface have such a linked Location, accessible via Document.location and Window.location respectively."]

properties.name: hash
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing a '#' followed by the fragment identifier of the URL.

properties.name: host
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing the host, that is the hostname, a ':', and the port of the URL.

properties.name: hostname
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing the domain of the URL.

properties.name: href
properties.overview: Is a stringifier that returns a USVString containing the entire URL. If changed, the associated document navigates to the new page. It can be set from a different origin than the associated document.

properties.name: origin
properties.overview: Returns a USVString containing the canonical form of the origin of the specific location.

properties.name: pathname
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing an initial '/' followed by the path of the URL.

properties.name: port
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing the port number of the URL.

properties.name: protocol
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing the protocol scheme of the URL, including the final ':'.

properties.name: search
properties.overview: Is a USVString containing a '?' followed by the parameters or "querystring" of the URL. Modern browsers provide URLSearchParams and URL.searchParams to make it easy to parse out the parameters from the querystring.

methods.name: assign
methods.overview: Loads the resource at the URL provided in parameter.

parameters.name: url
parameters.overview: Is a DOMString containing the URL of the page to navigate to.

methods.name: reload
methods.overview: Reloads the resource from the current URL. Its optional unique parameter is a Boolean, which, when it is true, causes the page to always be reloaded from the server. If it is false or not specified, the browser may reload the page from its cache.

methods.name: replace
methods.overview: Replaces the current resource with the one at the provided URL. The difference from the assign() method is that after using replace() the current page will not be saved in session History, meaning the user won't be able to use the back button to navigate to it.

parameters.name: url
parameters.overview: Is a DOMString containing the URL of the page to navigate to.

methods.name: toString
methods.overview: Returns a USVString containing the whole URL. It is a synonym for HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils.href, though it can't be used to modify the value.

name: MediaError
overview: ["The MediaError interface represents an error which occurred while handling media in an HTML media element based on HTMLMediaElement, such as element is used to embed sound content in documents. It may contain one or more audio sources, represented using the src attribute or the element: the browser will choose the most suitable one. It can also be the destination for streamed media, using a MediaStream.\"><audio> or ) embeds a media player which supports video playback into the document. You can use .","A MediaError object describes the error in general terms using a numeric code categorizing the kind of error, and a message, which provides specific diagnostics about what went wrong."]

properties.name: code
properties.overview:
A number which represents the general type of error that occurred, as follows:
Name Value Description
MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED 1 The fetching of the associated resource was aborted by the user's request.
MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK 2 Some kind of network error occurred which prevented the media from being successfully fetched, despite having previously been available.
MEDIA_ERR_DECODE 3 Despite having previously been determined to be usable, an error occurred while trying to decode the media resource, resulting in an error.
MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED 4 The associated resource or media provider object (such as a MediaStream) has been found to be unsuitable.

properties.name: message
properties.overview: A DOMString object containing a human-readable string which provides specific diagnostic information to help the reader understand the error condition which occurred; specifically, it isn't simply a summary of what the error code means, but actual diagnostic information to help in understanding what exactly went wrong. This text and its format is not defined by the specification and will vary from one user agent to another. If no diagnostics are available, or no explanation can be provided, this value is an empty string ("").

name: MediaList
overview: ["The MediaList interface represents the media queries of a stylesheet, e.g. those set using a ) specifies relationships between the current document and an external resource. This element is most commonly used to link to stylesheets, but is also used to establish site icons (both "favicon" style icons and icons for the home screen and apps on mobile devices) among other things.\"><link> element's media attribute."]

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Returns the number of media queries in the MediaList.

properties.name: mediaText
properties.overview: A stringifier that returns a DOMString representing the MediaList as text, and also allows you to set a new MediaList.

methods.name: appendMedium
methods.overview: Adds a media query to the MediaList.

methods.name: deleteMedium
methods.overview: Removes a media query from the MediaList.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: A getter that returns a CSSOMString representing a media query as text, given the media query's index value inside the MediaList.

name: MediaStream
overview: ["The MediaStream interface represents a stream of media content. A stream consists of several tracks such as video or audio tracks. Each track is specified as an instance of MediaStreamTrack.You can obtain a MediaStream object either by using the constructor or by calling MediaDevices.getUserMedia().","Some user agents subclass this interface to provide more precise information or functionality, like in CanvasCaptureMediaStream."]

properties.name: active
properties.overview: A Boolean value that returns true if the MediaStream is active, or false otherwise.

properties.name: id
properties.overview: A DOMString containing 36 characters denoting a universally unique identifier (UUID) for the object.

properties.name: onaddtrack
properties.overview: An EventHandler containing the action to perform when an addtrack event is fired when a new MediaStreamTrack object is added.

properties.name: onremovetrack
properties.overview: An EventHandler containing the action to perform when a removetrack event is fired when a MediaStreamTrack object is removed from it.

methods.name: addTrack
methods.overview: Stores a copy of the MediaStreamTrack given as argument. If the track has already been added to the MediaStream object, nothing happens.

methods.name: clone
methods.overview: Returns a clone of the MediaStream object. The clone will, however, have a unique value for id.

methods.name: getAudioTracks
methods.overview: Returns a list of the MediaStreamTrack objects stored in the MediaStream object that have their kind attribute set to audio. The order is not defined, and may not only vary from one browser to another, but also from one call to another.

methods.name: getTrackById
methods.overview: Returns the track whose ID corresponds to the one given in parameters, trackid. If no parameter is given, or if no track with that ID does exist, it returns null. If several tracks have the same ID, it returns the first one.

methods.name: getTracks
methods.overview: Returns a list of all MediaStreamTrack objects stored in the MediaStream object, regardless of the value of the kind attribute. The order is not defined, and may not only vary from one browser to another, but also from one call to another.

methods.name: getVideoTracks
methods.overview: Returns a list of the MediaStreamTrack objects stored in the MediaStream object that have their kind attribute set to "video". The order is not defined, and may not only vary from one browser to another, but also from one call to another.

methods.name: removeTrack
methods.overview: Removes the MediaStreamTrack given as argument. If the track is not part of the MediaStream object, nothing happens.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.

methods.overview: Dispatches an event to this EventTarget.

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.

name: NamedNodeMap
overview: ["The NamedNodeMap interface represents a collection of Attr objects. Objects inside a NamedNodeMap are not in any particular order, unlike NodeList, although they may be accessed by an index as in an array.","A NamedNodeMap object is live and will thus be auto-updated if changes are made to its contents internally or elsewhere."]

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Returns the amount of objects in the map.

methods.name: getNamedItem
methods.overview: Returns a Attr, corresponding to the given name.

parameters.name: qualifiedName
parameters.overview: name is the name of the desired attribute

methods.name: getNamedItemNS
methods.overview: Returns a Attr identified by a namespace and related local name.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: Returns the Attr at the given index, or null if the index is higher or equal to the number of nodes.

methods.name: removeNamedItem
methods.overview: Removes the Attr identified by the given map.

methods.name: removeNamedItemNS
methods.overview: Removes the Attr identified by the given namespace and related local name.

methods.name: setNamedItem
methods.overview: Replaces, or adds, the Attr identified in the map by the given name.

methods.name: setNamedItemNS
methods.overview: Replaces, or adds, the Attr identified in the map by the given namespace and related local name.

name: Node
overview: ["Node is an interface from which various types of DOM API objects inherit, allowing those types to be treated similarly; for example, inheriting the same set of methods, or being testable in the same way.","All of the following interfaces inherit the Node interface's methods and properties: Document, Element, Attr, CharacterData (which Text, Comment, and CDATASection inherit), ProcessingInstruction, DocumentFragment, DocumentType, Notation, Entity, EntityReference","Those interfaces may return null in certain cases where the methods and properties are not relevant. They may throw an exception — for example when adding children to a node type for which no children can exist."]

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: textContent

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.overview:

methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element has any child nodes.

name: NodeFilter
overview: ["A NodeFilter interface represents an object used to filter the nodes in a NodeIterator or TreeWalker. They don't know anything about the DOM or how to traverse nodes; they just know how to evaluate a single node against the provided filter."]

methods.name: acceptNode
methods.overview:
Returns an unsigned short that will be used to tell if a given Node must be accepted or not by the NodeIterator or TreeWalker iteration algorithm. This method is expected to be written by the user of a NodeFilter. Possible return values are:
Constant Description
FILTER_ACCEPT Value returned by the NodeFilter.acceptNode() method when a node should be accepted.
FILTER_REJECT Value to be returned by the NodeFilter.acceptNode() method when a node should be rejected. For TreeWalker, child nodes are also rejected. For NodeIterator, this flag is synonymous with FILTER_SKIP.
FILTER_SKIP Value to be returned by NodeFilter.acceptNode() for nodes to be skipped by the NodeIterator or TreeWalker object. The children of skipped nodes are still considered. This is treated as "skip this node but not its children".

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: Is a Node being the object to check against the filter.

name: NodeIterator
overview: ["The NodeIterator interface represents an iterator over the members of a list of the nodes in a subtree of the DOM. The nodes will be returned in document order."]

properties.name: filter
properties.overview: Returns a NodeFilter used to select the relevant nodes.

properties.name: pointerBeforeReferenceNode
properties.overview: Returns a Boolean flag that indicates whether the NodeIterator is anchored before, the flag being true, or after, the flag being false, the anchor node.

properties.name: referenceNode
properties.overview: Returns the Node to which the iterator is anchored.

properties.name: root
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the root node as specified when the NodeIterator was created.

properties.name: whatToShow
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned long being a bitmask made of constants describing the types of Node that must to be presented. Non-matching nodes are skipped, but their children may be included, if relevant.

The possible values are:

Constant Numerical value Description
NodeFilter.SHOW_ALL -1 (that is the max value of unsigned long) Shows all nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ATTRIBUTE 2 Shows attribute Attr nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a NodeIterator with an Attr node as its root; in this case, it means that the attribute node will appear in the first position of the iteration or traversal. Since attributes are never children of other nodes, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_CDATA_SECTION 8 Shows CDATASection nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_COMMENT 128 Shows Comment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT 256 Shows Document nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT 1024 Shows DocumentFragment nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_DOCUMENT_TYPE 512 Shows DocumentType nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT 1 Shows Element nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY 32 Shows Entity nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a NodeIterator with an Entity node as its root; in this case, it means that the Entity node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_ENTITY_REFERENCE 16 Shows EntityReference nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_NOTATION 2048 Shows Notation nodes. This is meaningful only when creating a NodeIterator with a Notation node as its root; in this case, it means that the Notation node will appear in the first position of the traversal. Since entities are not part of the document tree, they do not appear when traversing over the document tree.
NodeFilter.SHOW_PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION 64 Shows ProcessingInstruction nodes.
NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT 4 Shows Text nodes.

methods.name: detach
methods.overview: This operation is a no-op. It doesn't do anything. Previously it was telling the engine that the NodeIterator was no more used, but this is now useless.

methods.overview: Returns the next Node in the document, or null if there are none.

methods.name: previousNode
methods.overview: Returns the previous Node in the document, or null if there are none.

name: NodeList
overview: ["NodeList objects are collections of nodes, usually returned by properties such as Node.childNodes and methods such as document.querySelectorAll()."]

methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing code to go through all key/value pairs contained in the collection. (In this case, the keys are numbers starting from 0 and the values are nodes.)

methods.overview: Executes a provided function once per NodeList element, passing the element as an argument to the function.

parameters.overview: index is the index of the node to be fetched. The index is zero-based.

methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing code to go through all the keys of the key/value pairs contained in the collection. (In this case, the keys are numbers starting from 0.)

methods.name: values
methods.overview: Returns an iterator allowing code to go through all values (nodes) of the key/value pairs contained in the collection.

name: NonDocumentTypeChildNode
overview: ["The NonDocumentTypeChildNode interface contains methods that are particular to Node objects that can have a parent, but not suitable for DocumentType.","NonDocumentTypeChildNode is a raw interface and no object of this type can be created; it is implemented by Element, and CharacterData objects."]

properties.name: nextElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately following this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list following this node.

properties.name: previousElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately prior to this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list prior to this node.

name: OffscreenCanvas
overview:
["This is an experimental technology
Check the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production."]

properties.overview: The height of the offscreen canvas.

properties.name: width
properties.overview: The width of the offscreen canvas.

methods.name: convertToBlob
methods.overview: Creates a Blob object representing the image contained in the canvas.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
You can specify several options when converting your OffscreenCanvas object into a Blob object, for example:

const blob = offscreenCanvas.convertToBlob({
  type: "image/jpeg",
  quality: 0.95
});

options:

  • type: A DOMString indicating the image format. The default type is image/png.
  • quality: A Number between 0 and 1 indicating image quality if the type option is image/jpeg or image/webp. If this argument is anything else, the default value for image quality is used. Other arguments are ignored.

methods.name: getContext
methods.overview: Returns a rendering context for the offscreen canvas.

parameters.name: contextId
parameters.overview:
Is a DOMString containing the context identifier defining the drawing context associated to the canvas. Possible values are:
  • "2d" creates a CanvasRenderingContext2D object representing a two-dimensional rendering context.
  • "webgl" creates a WebGLRenderingContext object representing a three-dimensional rendering context. This context is only available on browsers that implement WebGL version 1 (OpenGL ES 2.0).
  • "webgl2" creates a WebGL2RenderingContext object representing a three-dimensional rendering context. This context is only available on browsers that implement WebGL version 2 (OpenGL ES 3.0).

  • "bitmaprenderer" creates a ImageBitmapRenderingContext which only provides functionality to replace the content of the canvas with a given ImageBitmap.

Note: The identifiers "experimental-webgl" or "experimental-webgl2" are also used in implementations of WebGL. These implementations have not reached test suite conformance, or the graphic drivers situation on the platform is not yet stable. The Khronos Group certifies WebGL implementations under certain conformance rules.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
You can use several context attributes when creating your rendering context, for example:

offscreen.getContext("webgl", 
                 { antialias: false,
                   depth: false });
2d context attributes:
  • alpha: Boolean that indicates if the canvas contains an alpha channel. If set to false, the browser now knows that the backdrop is always opaque, which can speed up drawing of transparent content and images then.
  • (Gecko only) willReadFrequently: Boolean that indicates whether or not a lot of read-back operations are planned. This will force the use of a software (instead of hardware accelerated) 2D canvas and can save memory when calling getImageData() frequently. This option is only available, if the flag gfx.canvas.willReadFrequently.enable is set to true (which, by default, is only the case for B2G/Firefox OS).
  • (Blink only) storage: String that indicates which storage is used ("persistent" by default).
WebGL context attributes:
  • alpha: Boolean that indicates if the canvas contains an alpha buffer.
  • depth: Boolean that indicates that the drawing buffer has a depth buffer of at least 16 bits.
  • stencil: Boolean that indicates that the drawing buffer has a stencil buffer of at least 8 bits.
  • antialias: Boolean that indicates whether or not to perform anti-aliasing.
  • premultipliedAlpha: Boolean that indicates that the page compositor will assume the drawing buffer contains colors with pre-multiplied alpha.
  • preserveDrawingBuffer: If the value is true the buffers will not be cleared and will preserve their values until cleared or overwritten by the author.

  • failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat: Boolean that indicates if a context will be created if the system performance is low.

It's implemented by Element, Document, and DocumentFragment objects.","See Locating DOM elements using selectors to learn how to use CSS selectors to find nodes or elements of interest."]

properties.name: childElementCount
properties.overview: Returns the number of children of this ParentNode which are elements.

properties.name: children
properties.overview: Returns a live HTMLCollection containing all of the Element objects that are children of this ParentNode, omitting all of its non-element nodes.

properties.name: firstElementChild
properties.overview: Returns the first node which is both a child of this ParentNode and is also an Element, or null if there is none.

properties.name: lastElementChild
properties.overview: Returns the last node which is both a child of this ParentNode and is an Element, or null if there is none.

methods.name: append
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects after the last child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: prepend
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node objects or DOMString objects before the first child of the ParentNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: One or more nodes to insert before the first child node currently in the ParentNode. Each node can be specified as either a Node object or as a string; strings are inserted as new Text nodes.

methods.name: querySelector
methods.overview: Returns the first Element with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid compound selector list supported by the browser; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

methods.name: querySelectorAll
methods.overview: Returns a NodeList representing a list of elements with the current element as root that matches the specified group of selectors.

parameters.name: selectors
parameters.overview: A DOMString containing one or more selectors to match against. This string must be a valid CSS selector string; if it's not, a SyntaxError exception is thrown. See Locating DOM elements using selectors for more information about using selectors to identify elements. Multiple selectors may be specified by separating them using commas.

name: ProcessingInstruction
overview: ["The ProcessingInstruction interface represents a processing instruction; that is, a Node which embeds an instruction targeting a specific application but that can be ignored by any other applications which don't recognize the instruction.","A processing instruction is different from the XML declaration."]

properties.name: target
properties.overview: A name identifying the application to which the instruction is targeted,

properties.name: data
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the textual data contained in this object.

properties.name: length
properties.overview: Returns an unsigned long representing the size of the string contained in CharacterData.data.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

properties.name: nodeType
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned short representing the type of the node. Possible values are:
Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.name: nodeValue
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the value of the current node.

properties.name: ownerDocument
properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: previousSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the previous node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: textContent
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the textual content of an element and all its descendants.

properties.name: nextElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately following this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list following this node.

properties.name: previousElementSibling
properties.overview: Returns the Element immediately prior to this node in its parent's children list, or null if there is no Element in the list prior to this node.

methods.name: appendData
methods.overview: Appends the given DOMString to the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the concatenated DOMString.

methods.name: deleteData
methods.overview: Removes the specified amount of characters, starting at the specified offset, from the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the shortened DOMString.

methods.name: insertData
methods.overview: Inserts the specified characters, at the specified offset, in the CharacterData.data string; when this method returns, data contains the modified DOMString.

methods.name: replaceData
methods.overview: Replaces the specified amount of characters, starting at the specified offset, with the specified DOMString; when this method returns, data contains the modified DOMString.

methods.name: substringData
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the part of CharacterData.data of the specified length and starting at the specified offset.

methods.name: appendChild
methods.overview:
Adds the specified childNode argument as the last child to the current node.
If the argument referenced an existing node on the DOM tree, the node will be detached from its current position and attached at the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to append to the given parent node (commonly an element).

methods.name: cloneNode
methods.overview: Clone a Node, and optionally, all of its contents. By default, it clones the content of the node.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.overview:
If true, then node and its whole subtree—including text that may be in child Text nodes—is also copied.

If false, only node will be cloned. Any text that node contains is not cloned, either (since text is contained by one or more child Text nodes).

deep has no effect on empty elements (such as the <img> and <input> elements).

*Note: In the DOM4 specification (since Gecko 13.0 (Firefox 13 / Thunderbird 13 / SeaMonkey 2.10)), the optional deep argument defaults to true. 

This behavior has been changed in the latest spec! Although deep it still optional, it now defaults to false.

You should always provide an explicit value for backward and forward compatibility.

  • With Gecko 28.0 (Firefox 28 / Thunderbird 28 / SeaMonkey 2.25 / Firefox OS 1.3)), the console warned developers not to omit the argument.
  • Starting with Gecko 29.0 (Firefox 29 / Thunderbird 29 / SeaMonkey 2.26)), a shallow clone is defaulted instead of a deep clone.

methods.name: compareDocumentPosition
methods.overview: Compares the position of the current node against another node in any other document.

parameters.name: other
parameters.overview: The other Node with which to compare the first node’s document position.

methods.name: contains
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not a node is a descendant of the calling node.

methods.name: getRootNode
methods.overview: Returns the context object's root which optionally includes the shadow root if it is available.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
An object that sets options for getting the root node. The available options are:
  • composed: A Boolean that indicates whether the shadow root should be returned (false, the default), or a root node beyond shadow root (true).

methods.name: hasChildNodes
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean indicating whether or not the element has any child nodes.

methods.name: insertBefore
methods.overview: Inserts a Node before the reference node as a child of a specified parent node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The node to be inserted.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The node before which newNode is inserted. If this is null, then newNode is inserted at the end of parentNode's child nodes.

methods.name: isDefaultNamespace
methods.overview: Accepts a namespace URI as an argument and returns a Boolean with a value of true if the namespace is the default namespace on the given node or false if not.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.overview: namespaceURI is a string representing the namespace against which the element will be checked.

methods.name: isEqualNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean which indicates whether or not two nodes are of the same type and all their defining data points match.

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode: The Node to compare equality with.

methods.name: isSameNode
methods.overview: Returns a Boolean value indicating whether or not the two nodes are the same (that is, they reference the same object).

parameters.name: otherNode
parameters.overview: otherNode The Node to test against.

methods.name: lookupNamespaceURI
methods.overview: Accepts a prefix and returns the namespace URI associated with it on the given node if found (and null if not). Supplying null for the prefix will return the default namespace.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.overview: The prefix to look for. If this parameter is null, the method will return the default namespace URI, if any.

methods.name: lookupPrefix
methods.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the prefix for a given namespace URI, if present, and null if not. When multiple prefixes are possible, the result is implementation-dependent.

methods.name: normalize
methods.overview: Clean up all the text nodes under this element (merge adjacent, remove empty).

methods.name: removeChild
methods.overview: Removes a child node from the current element, which must be a child of the current node.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: child is the child node to be removed from the DOM.

methods.name: replaceChild
methods.overview: Replaces one child Node of the current one with the second one given in parameter.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The new node to replace oldChild. If it already exists in the DOM, it is first removed.

parameters.name: child
parameters.overview: The child to be replaced.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.overview: Registers an event handler of a specific event type on the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A case-sensitive string representing the event type to listen for.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The object that receives a notification (an object that implements the Event interface) when an event of the specified type occurs. This must be an object implementing the EventListener interface, or a JavaScript function. See The event listener callback for details on the callback itself.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object specifies characteristics about the event listener. The available options are:
    capture
    A Boolean indicating that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    once
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be invoked at most once after being added. If true, the listener would be automatically removed when invoked.
    passive
    A Boolean that, if true, indicates that the function specified by listener will never call preventDefault(). If a passive listener does call preventDefault(), the user agent will do nothing other than generate a console warning. See Improving scrolling performance with passive listeners to learn more.
    mozSystemGroup
    A Boolean indicating that the listener should be added to the system group. Available only in code running in XBL or in the chrome of the Firefox browser.
  • A Boolean indicating whether events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree. Events that are bubbling upward through the tree will not trigger a listener designated to use capture. Event bubbling and capturing are two ways of propagating events that occur in an element that is nested within another element, when both elements have registered a handle for that event. The event propagation mode determines the order in which elements receive the event. See DOM Level 3 Events and JavaScript Event order for a detailed explanation. If not specified, useCapture defaults to false.
    Note: For event listeners attached to the event target, the event is in the target phase, rather than the capturing and bubbling phases. Events in the target phase will trigger all listeners on an element in the order they were registered, regardless of the useCapture parameter.
    Note: useCapture has not always been optional. Ideally, you should include it for the widest possible browser compatibility.

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.overview: Dispatches an event to this EventTarget.

parameters.name: event
parameters.overview: event is the Event object to be dispatched.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.overview: Removes an event listener from the EventTarget.

parameters.name: type
parameters.overview: A string which specifies the type of event for which to remove an event listener.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.overview: The EventListener function of the event handler to remove from the event target.

parameters.name: options
parameters.overview:
• An options object that specifies characteristics about the event listener.

    The available options are:

    • capture: A Boolean which indicates that events of this type will be dispatched to the registered listener before being dispatched to any EventTarget beneath it in the DOM tree.
    •  mozSystemGroup: A Boolean available only for code running in XBL or in Firefox's chrome which indicates if the listener will be added to the system group.
  • Specifies whether the EventListener to be removed is registered as a capturing listener or not. If this parameter is absent, a default value of false is assumed.If a listener is registered twice, one with capture and one without, remove each one separately. Removal of a capturing listener does not affect a non-capturing version of the same listener, and vice versa.

methods.name: after
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just after this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: before
methods.overview: Inserts a set of Node or DOMString objects in the children list of this ChildNode's parent, just before this ChildNode. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to insert.

methods.name: remove
methods.overview: Removes this ChildNode from the children list of its parent.

methods.name: replaceWith
methods.overview: Replaces this ChildNode in the children list of its parent with a set of Node or DOMString objects. DOMString objects are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.overview: A set of Node or DOMString objects to replace.

name: RadioNodeList
overview: ["The RadioNodeList interface represents a collection of radio elements in a element represents a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information.\"><form> or a element is used to group several controls as well as labels ( element."]

properties.name: value
properties.overview: If the underlying element collection contains radio buttons, the value property represents the checked radio button. On retrieving the value property, the value of the currently checked radio button is returned as a string. If the collection does not contain any radio buttons or none of the radio buttons in the collection is in checked state, the empty string is returned. On setting the value property, the first radio button input element whose value property is equal to the new value will be set to checked.

properties.name: length
properties.overview: The number of nodes in the NodeList.

methods.name: entries
methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing code to go through all key/value pairs contained in the collection. (In this case, the keys are numbers starting from 0 and the values are nodes.)

methods.name: forEach
methods.overview: Executes a provided function once per NodeList element, passing the element as an argument to the function.

methods.name: item
methods.overview: Returns an item in the list by its index, or null if the index is out-of-bounds.

parameters.name: index
parameters.overview: index is the index of the node to be fetched. The index is zero-based.

methods.name: keys
methods.overview: Returns an iterator, allowing code to go through all the keys of the key/value pairs contained in the collection. (In this case, the keys are numbers starting from 0.)

methods.name: values
methods.overview: Returns an iterator allowing code to go through all values (nodes) of the key/value pairs contained in the collection.

name: Range
overview: ["The Range interface represents a fragment of a document that can contain nodes and parts of text nodes.","A range can be created by using the Document.createRange() method. Range objects can also be retrieved by using the getRangeAt() method of the Selection object or the caretRangeFromPoint() method of the Document object.","There also is the Range() constructor available."]

properties.name: commonAncestorContainer
properties.overview: Returns the deepest Node that contains the startContainer and endContainer nodes.

properties.name: collapsed
properties.overview: A Boolean value which is true if the range is collapsed. A collapsed range is one whose start position and end position are the same, resulting in a zero-character-long range.

properties.name: endContainer
properties.overview: The DOM Node in which the end of the range, as specified by the endOffset property, is located.

properties.name: endOffset
properties.overview: An integer value indicating the offset, in characters, from the beginning of the node's contents to the beginning of the range represented by the range object. This value must be less than the length of the endContainer node.

properties.name: startContainer
properties.overview: The DOM Node in which the beginning of the range, as specified by the startOffset property, is located.

properties.name: startOffset
properties.overview: An integer value indicating the offset, in characters, from the beginning of the node's contents to the last character of the contents referred to  by the range object. This value must be less than the length of the node indicated in startContainer.

methods.name: cloneContents
methods.overview: Returns a DocumentFragment copying the nodes of a Range.

methods.name: cloneRange
methods.overview: Returns a Range object with boundary points identical to the cloned Range.

methods.name: collapse
methods.overview: Collapses the Range to one of its boundary points.

parameters.name: toStart
parameters.overview: A Boolean value: true collapses the Range to its start, false to its end. If omitted, it defaults to false .

methods.name: compareBoundaryPoints
methods.overview: Compares the boundary points of the Range with another Range.

parameters.name: how
parameters.overview:
A constant describing the comparison method:
  • Range.END_TO_END compares the end boundary-point of sourceRange to the end boundary-point of Range.
  • Range.END_TO_START compares the end boundary-point of sourceRange to the start boundary-point of Range.
  • Range.START_TO_END compares the start boundary-point of sourceRange to the end boundary-point of Range.
  • Range.START_TO_START compares the start boundary-point of sourceRange to the start boundary-point of Range.

If the value of the parameter is invalid, a DOMException with a NotSupportedError code is thrown.

parameters.name: sourceRange
parameters.overview: A Range to compare boundary points with the range.

methods.name: comparePoint
methods.overview: Returns -1, 0, or 1 indicating whether the point occurs before, inside, or after the Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to compare with the Range.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.overview: An integer greater than or equal to zero representing the offset inside the referenceNode.

methods.name: createContextualFragment
methods.overview: Returns a DocumentFragment created from a given string of code.

parameters.name: fragment
parameters.overview: Text that contains text and tags to be converted to a document fragment.

methods.name: deleteContents
methods.overview: Removes the contents of a Range from the Document.

methods.name: detach
methods.overview: Releases the Range from use to improve performance.

methods.name: extractContents
methods.overview: Moves contents of a Range from the document tree into a DocumentFragment.

methods.name: getBoundingClientRect
methods.overview: Returns a DOMRect object which bounds the entire contents of the Range; this would be the union of all the rectangles returned by range.getClientRects().

methods.name: getClientRects
methods.overview: Returns a list of DOMRect objects that aggregates the results of Element.getClientRects() for all the elements in the Range.

methods.name: insertNode
methods.overview: Insert a Node at the start of a Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to insert at the start of the range.

methods.name: intersectsNode
methods.overview: Returns a boolean indicating whether the given node intersects the Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to compare with the Range.

methods.name: isPointInRange
methods.overview: Returns a boolean indicating whether the given point is in the Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to compare with the Range.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.overview: The offset into Node of the point to compare with the Range.

methods.name: selectNode
methods.overview: Sets the Range to contain the Node and its contents.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to select within a Range.

methods.name: selectNodeContents
methods.overview: Sets the Range to contain the contents of a Node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node whose contents will be selected within a Range.

methods.name: setEnd
methods.overview: Sets the end position of a Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node inside which the Range should end.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.overview: An integer greater than or equal to zero representing the offset for the end of the Range from the start of endNode.

methods.name: setEndAfter
methods.overview: Sets the end position of a Range relative to another Node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to end the Range after.

methods.name: setEndBefore
methods.overview: Sets the end position of a Range relative to another Node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to end the Range before.

methods.name: setStart
methods.overview: Sets the start position of a Range.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node where the Range should start.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.overview: An integer greater than or equal to zero representing the offset for the start of the Range from the start of startNode.

methods.name: setStartAfter
methods.overview: Sets the start position of a Range relative to another Node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node to start the Range after.

methods.name: setStartBefore
methods.overview: Sets the start position of a Range relative to another Node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.overview: The Node before which the Range should start.

methods.name: surroundContents
methods.overview: Moves content of a Range into a new Node.

parameters.name: newParent
parameters.overview: A Node with which to surround the contents.

methods.name: toString
methods.overview: Returns the text of the Range.

properties.name: body
properties.overview: A simple getter used to expose a ReadableStream of the body contents.

properties.name: bodyUsed
properties.overview: A Boolean that indicates whether the body has been read.

methods.name: arrayBuffer
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with an ArrayBuffer.

methods.name: blob
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a Blob.

methods.name: formData
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a FormData object.

methods.name: json
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with the result of parsing the body text as JSON.

methods.name: text
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a USVString (text). The response is always decoded using UTF-8.

name: Response
overview: ["The Response interface of the Fetch API represents the response to a request.","You can create a new Response object using the Response.Response() constructor, but you are more likely to encounter a Response object being returned as the result of another API operation—for example, a service worker Fetchevent.respondWith, or a simple GlobalFetch.fetch()."]

properties.name: headers
properties.overview: The Headers object associated with the response.

properties.name: ok
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200–299) or not.

properties.name: redirected
properties.overview: Indicates whether or not the response is the result of a redirect (that is, its URL list has more than one entry).

properties.name: status
properties.overview: The status code of the response. (This will be 200 for a success).

properties.name: statusText
properties.overview: The status message corresponding to the status code. (e.g., OK for 200).

properties.name: type
properties.overview: The type of the response (e.g., basic, cors).

properties.name: url
properties.overview: The URL of the response.

properties.name: body
properties.overview: A simple getter used to expose a ReadableStream of the body contents.

properties.name: bodyUsed
properties.overview: A Boolean that indicates whether the body has been read.

methods.name: clone
methods.overview: Creates a clone of a Response object.

methods.name: error
methods.overview: Returns a new Response object associated with a network error.

methods.name: redirect
methods.overview: Creates a new response with a different URL.

parameters.name: url
parameters.overview: The URL that the new response is to originate from.

parameters.name: status
parameters.overview: An optional status code for the response (e.g., 302.)

methods.name: arrayBuffer
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with an ArrayBuffer.

methods.name: blob
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a Blob.

methods.name: formData
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a FormData object.

methods.name: json
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with the result of parsing the body text as JSON.

methods.name: text
methods.overview: Takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise that resolves with a USVString (text). The response is always decoded using UTF-8.

name: SVGAnimatedLength
overview: ["The SVGAnimatedLength interface is used for attributes of basic type <length> which can be animated."]

properties.name: animVal
properties.overview: If the given attribute or property is being animated, contains the current animated value of the attribute or property. If the given attribute or property is not currently being animated, contains the same value as baseVal.

properties.name: baseVal
properties.overview: The base value of the given attribute before applying any animations.

name: SVGAnimatedTransformList
overview: ["The SVGAnimatedTransformList interface is used for attributes which take a list of numbers and which can be animated."]

properties.name: animVal
properties.overview: A read only SVGTransformList representing the current animated value of the given attribute. If the given attribute is not currently being animated, then the SVGTransformList will have the same contents as baseVal. The object referenced by animVal will always be distinct from the one referenced by baseVal, even when the attribute is not animated.

properties.name: baseVal
properties.overview: The base value of the given attribute before applying any animations.

name: SVGElement
overview: ["All of the SVG DOM interfaces that correspond directly to elements in the SVG language derive from the SVGElement interface."]

properties.name: attributes
properties.overview: Returns a NamedNodeMap object containing the assigned attributes of the corresponding HTML element.

properties.name: classList
properties.overview: Returns a DOMTokenList containing the list of class attributes.

properties.name: className
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the class of the element.

properties.name: clientHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner height of the element.

properties.name: clientLeft
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the left border of the element.

properties.name: clientTop
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the width of the top border of the element.

properties.name: clientWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the inner width of the element.

properties.name: id
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the id of the element.

properties.name: innerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element's content.

properties.name: localName
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the local part of the qualified name of the element.

properties.name: namespaceURI
properties.overview:
The namespace URI of the element, or null if it is no namespace.

Note: In Firefox 3.5 and earlier, HTML elements are in no namespace. In later versions, HTML elements are in the http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml namespace in both HTML and XML trees.

properties.name: onfullscreenchange
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenchange event, which is sent when the element enters or exits full-screen mode. This can be used to watch both for successful expected transitions, but also to watch for unexpected changes, such as when your app is running in the background.

properties.name: onfullscreenerror
properties.overview: An event handler for the fullscreenerror event, which is sent when an error occurs while attempting to change into full-screen mode.

properties.name: outerHTML
properties.overview: Is a DOMString representing the markup of the element including its content. When used as a setter, replaces the element with nodes parsed from the given string.

properties.name: part
properties.overview: Represents the part identifier(s) of the element (i.e. set using the part attribute), returned as a DOMTokenList.

properties.name: prefix
properties.overview: A DOMString representing the namespace prefix of the element, or null if no prefix is specified.

properties.name: scrollHeight
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view height of an element.

properties.name: scrollLeft
properties.overview: Is a Number representing the left scroll offset of the element.

properties.name: scrollTop
properties.overview: A Number representing number of pixels the top of the document is scrolled vertically.

properties.name: scrollWidth
properties.overview: Returns a Number representing the scroll view width of the element.

properties.name: shadowRoot
properties.overview: Returns the open shadow root that is hosted by the element, or null if no open shadow root is present.

properties.name: slot
properties.overview: Returns the name of the shadow DOM slot the element is inserted in.

properties.name: tagName
properties.overview: Returns a String with the name of the tag for the given element.

properties.name: baseURI
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString representing the base URL of the document containing the Node.

properties.name: childNodes
properties.overview: Returns a live NodeList containing all the children of this node. NodeList being live means that if the children of the Node change, the NodeList object is automatically updated.

properties.name: firstChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the first direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: isConnected
properties.overview: A boolean indicating whether or not the Node is connected (directly or indirectly) to the context object, e.g. the Document object in the case of the normal DOM, or the ShadowRoot in the case of a shadow DOM.

properties.name: lastChild
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the last direct child node of the node, or null if the node has no child.

properties.name: nextSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the next node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: nodeName
properties.overview: Returns a DOMString containing the name of the Node. The structure of the name will differ with the node type. E.g. An HTMLElement will contain the name of the corresponding tag, like 'audio' for an HTMLAudioElement, a Text node will have the '#text' string, or a Document node will have the '#document' string.

properties.name: nodeType
properties.overview:
Returns an unsigned short representing the type of the node. Possible values are:
Name Value
ELEMENT_NODE 1
ATTRIBUTE_NODE  2
TEXT_NODE 3
CDATA_SECTION_NODE 4
ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE  5
ENTITY_NODE  6
PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE 7
COMMENT_NODE 8
DOCUMENT_NODE 9
DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE 10
DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE 11
NOTATION_NODE  12

properties.name: nodeValue
properties.overview: Returns / Sets the value of the current node.

properties.name: ownerDocument
properties.overview: Returns the Document that this node belongs to. If the node is itself a document, returns null.

properties.name: parentElement
properties.overview: Returns an Element that is the parent of this node. If the node has no parent, or if that parent is not an Element, this property returns null.

properties.name: parentNode
properties.overview: Returns a Node that is the parent of this node. If there is no such node, like if this node is the top of the tree or if doesn't participate in a tree, this property returns null.

properties.name: previousSibling
properties.overview: Returns a Node representing the previous node in the tree, or null if there isn't such node.

properties.name: textContent

properties.name: style

When getting, it returns a CSSStyleDeclaration object that contains a list of all styles properties for that element with values assigned for the attributes that are defined in the element's inline style attribute.
